item.title: Terrion Arnold Arrested: Lions CB Faces Life in Prison
item.description:
How does a first-round NFL draft pick go from reporting a $200,000 theft to facing the possibility of life in prison? That is the stunning question now surrounding Terrion Arnold, the Detroit Lions cornerback who turned himself in to a Tampa jail on multiple felony counts.

Quick Summary

  • Terrion Arnold, 23, was arrested in connection with a February 2026 armed robbery and kidnapping in Tampa, Florida.
  • He faces four counts of kidnapping and four counts of armed robbery, charges that carry a potential maximum sentence of life in prison.
  • Prosecutors allege Arnold orchestrated a retaliation plot after reporting a theft from his rental property.
  • The Detroit Lions said they “will not comment at this time out of respect for the ongoing legal process.”

The arrest of a young, rising defensive starter is one of the most serious off-field developments the Lions have faced in years. Let’s break down exactly what investigators say happened, what the charges mean, and what it could mean for Detroit’s 2026 season.

item.title: Andrus Peat: The NFL Veteran Who Paved the Way for Arizona's Koa Peat
item.description:
As the Arizona Wildcats stormed into the 2026 Final Four, all eyes turned to freshman sensation Koa Peat. But behind every great athlete, there’s often a trailblazer who came first. For Koa, that trailblazer is his eldest brother Andrus Peat — a first-round NFL draft pick who spent over a decade protecting some of football’s biggest names.

Key Takeaways

  • Andrus Peat was the 13th overall pick in the 2015 NFL Draft by the New Orleans Saints
  • He played 11 seasons in the NFL across three teams: Saints, Raiders, and Steelers
  • The Peat family has seven siblings, all with athletic backgrounds
  • Father Todd Peat Sr. also played in the NFL for seven years
  • Koa Peat, the youngest sibling, is now a standout on Arizona’s Final Four basketball team

Andrus Peat’s NFL Journey: From Stanford to the Pros

Andrus Peat’s path to professional football started at Stanford University, where he developed into one of the top offensive line prospects in college football. He chose to forego his final season of eligibility to enter the 2015 NFL Draft — a decision that paid off handsomely.
